thesis: Eaton has genuine organic demand and improving FCF, but the bear carries the acquisition-return hurdle at an estimated 27.40x forward multiple. Debt more than doubled to $20.611bn against $0.695bn cash/investments, while segment margin fell 80bp and adjusted EPS excludes material costs. Profitable 14% organic growth and backlog expansion retain upside, so the observed tradeoff supports waiting rather than declaring acquisition failure.
strongest_counterexample: H1 FCF increased from $0.807bn to $1.188bn despite higher capex, and 23.1% segment margin remains profitable; the existing engine supplies a real base for successful integration.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable H1 FCF above $1.188bn with total debt below $20.611bn and segment margin at least 23.1% would weaken the acquisition-financing objection.
Comparable H1 FCF at or below zero or segment margin below the observed 23.1% with debt still rising would invalidate the retained funded-growth counterweight.
decisive_factors: $11.079bn acquisition payments are separate investing spend, not recurring capex.
Organic growth is accepted, but a larger funding burden and nearly flat prospective GAAP EPS balance it; an undrawn revolver is not cash.
